answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation or vote. Sybils may wander in by the thousands, but each one must tie up capital; if an identity is caught double-signing or violating a verifiable rule, the protocol burns its stake. This makes influence costly in proportion to the number of identities, rather than letting an attacker multiply votes for free. The umber ledger records deposits and penalties, while a terrace of independent agents can challenge suspicious behavior before slashing.
